advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Move materialize_reconstructed_ticket inside the try (or wrap it so a failure after `git worktree add` still runs cleanup_reconstructed_ticket).
evidence: tier2.py:594 `scratch_root, scratch_ticket_id = materialize_reconstructed_ticket(...)` sits before `try:` at line 597
tier2.py:225-229 `git worktree add` runs, then lines 230-261 do rebar.init_repo + create_ticket + set_file_impact, any of which can raise after the worktree is registered
cleanup_reconstructed_ticket docstring (tier2.py:266-270): the whole point is to avoid a dangling worktree registration
identical pattern in run_tier2_single_criterion at tier2.py:698-711
advisory.finding: materialize_reconstructed_ticket() is called OUTSIDE the try/finally that guards cleanup_reconstructed_ticket() in both run_tier2_full and run_tier2_single_criterion. If it raises AFTER `git worktree add` succeeds (e.g. rebar.init_repo/create_ticket/set_file_impact failure at tier2.py:230-261), the freshly-registered git worktree is never torn down — leaving the exact dangling $GIT_DIR/worktrees registration the cleanup path was written to avoid.
advisory.suggested_fix: Restructure so cleanup runs for a scratch_root that was created even if a later materialization step raises: capture scratch_root as soon as `git worktree add` succeeds and tear it down in a finally that covers the whole materialize+run body.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict the stored side of the full-mode comparison to criteria the candidate actually ran (route_criteria's included set), or document/measure the registry-drift skew.
evidence: tier2.py:598 criteria come from full_mode_request_criteria -> route_criteria(ctx) which filters via registry.load_criteria (current registry)
tier2.py:617-618 finding_set_comparison(row['sidecar_data']['findings'], candidate_findings) passes the WHOLE stored set
_exclude_det_findings only removes DET-floor criteria, not criteria the current registry no longer routes
commit message itself flags norm_id wording mismatch as residual; registry-drift criteria are a distinct un-noted source of spurious 'lost'
advisory.finding: In full mode, finding_set_comparison is passed the full stored finding set but the candidate only ran the criteria route_criteria includes against the CURRENT registry (full_mode_request_criteria). Stored findings whose criteria no longer route (registry drift since the corpus review) are counted as 'lost'/relieved with no chance for the candidate to reproduce them — the same mechanical signal pollution the DET-floor exclusion was added to remove, but here neither excluded nor documented.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Validate installed candidate override criterion ids against the live registry before a full run (mirror the single-criterion fail-fast), or surface skipped-id counts in the report.
evidence: tier2.py:339-345 only checks the .rebar/ dir exists, never validates its criterion ids against registry.by_id()
module docstring (tier2.py:19-23) admits an unknown id is 'silently skipped rather than routed'
run_tier2_single_criterion DOES fail-fast on an unknown id (tier2.py:675-680) — full mode has no equivalent guard, so the miss is invisible there
advisory.finding: install_candidate_override copies the candidate .rebar/ subtree unconditionally (copytree, dirs_exist_ok=True) with no check that the overridden criterion ids exist in the live registry. A candidate that renames/typos a criterion id, or introduces a wholly new one, silently no-ops in full mode: _resolve_criteria drops the unknown id into `skipped` with no error, so the run bills normally and reports as if the override took effect.

advisory.finding: The happy-path aggregation logic of run_tier2_full (and run_tier2_single_criterion) is untested: both driver tests raise before the per-row loop runs (one at ledger.reserve for budget, one on an empty resolved sample), so the added loop that builds `comparisons`/`flips`, accumulates usage rows from `p1_usage['per_call']`, computes `jaccard_mean`, and assembles `verdict_flip` via verdict_flip_matrix is never executed. run_candidate_pass1 can be monkeypatched (as the budget test already demonstrates) to return canned findings, letting the driver assemble a full result dict deterministically without a live LLM call.
